# R268 — Prefill scratch retirement and packed-native decode-cache growth

Date: 2026-10-12 (JST). Read-only source audit of integrated WN `sync-xe-v0143-nonfinite-20261012`, HEAD `0691bcdf5af63a85b3b25650f367d3276db64035`, with the committed report registry v161 and prior R136/R247/R251/R264/R266 evidence. No source or worktree edits, build, test, model/GPU/process run, active Main-log read, Git mutation, or cleanup. No new measurements were collected. The supplied B570 values are context, not independently validated here. Full context remains 262,144; no setting or output status is changed.

## Finding

In the ordinary generation caller, the stack-local `strata::prefill::Prefill prefill` remains alive after the batched prompt, lent-slot refill, residency-map upload, and prefill-stat print, through the per-token decode loop. There is no caller `reset()` at this boundary. `Prefill::reset()` is the available public teardown/reinitialize operation; there is no public `release()` or `ready()` method. It clears `stats_`, so a caller must copy `PrefillStats` before reset if it still needs them. It resets the implementation to a new empty `Impl`; callers must `init()` again before another run.

The owned-allocation prefill route is the direct memory-release candidate: `Prefill::Impl::release` frees `impl_->owned`, CPU scratch, host/event resources, and its copy stream after queue drains. When the prompt borrows expert-cache slots, those slot bytes belong to `ExpertCache`; `reset()` does not free the cache backing, and the caller has already refilled those slots for decode. Thus only actual owned Prefill scratch (plus helper allocations) is returned to the allocator. A reset alone does not enlarge the decode cache.

## Teardown and completion contract

`release()` first cancels the stager, then passes `stream_sync(cs)` and `stream_sync(copy)` through `publication::cleanup_require` before resetting the stager or freeing scratch. A failed sync is fail-stop (`_Exit(74)` in the cleanup helper); it is not silently ignored and cannot continue into a supposedly safe reuse. After successful drains, the stager is joined and its event-gated source work is retired. The caller-owned `cs` is synchronized but not destroyed. `stream_destroy`, event destruction, and `gpu::free` are void interfaces here, so `reset()` does not return a checked allocator-release result; successful queue synchronization establishes the in-flight-work boundary, not a measured free-byte delta or proof every teardown call succeeded.

Do not replace this with an unchecked `init()` over a live `Impl`: the observed API has no ready guard, and live resources would need to be retired first. Any future interface should expose an explicit initialized state and a checked teardown outcome, while preserving the existing fail-stop rule when queue completion is unknown.

## Two different implementation seams

**A. Retire Prefill scratch only (lowest-risk boundary).** After successful `prefill.run`, all lent cache slots have been refilled, `xcache.sync_queued` succeeded, `host_res` has been restored, and `d_res` has been uploaded; after copying the stats needed for reporting, reset the owned-buffer `Prefill` before entering the first decode token. Keep `SessionState`, the cache, residency maps, K/V and GDN/PLE state, MTP state, verifier, and all graph owners alive. The token/decode graphs capture session/cache data, not Prefill's temporary chunk buffers; the prompt callback and `draft_kv` use are over when `run` returns. Retain the existing 262,144 context and all event/queue completion checks. This seam can return owned scratch to the allocator but makes no promise about which allocation claims it next.

The persistent server has a different lifetime: its staged Prefill objects are initialized once and reused across requests. A permanent reset would require reinitialization before the next prompt and must occur only after the entire prompt batch, callback/MTP prompt work, refill, and publication are complete. It is not useful for freeing borrowed cache slots while the cache remains allocated. Any server version would need a request-boundary lifecycle and lazy/reusable re-init contract, not a per-chunk reset.

**B. Replace or enlarge cache after scratch retirement (higher-risk transaction).** Current `ExpertCache::grow(want_bytes)` can only map segments in the fixed address reservation established at `open/open_sized`; it cannot exceed `full_bytes()`. `--vram-elastic` reserves the requested full range and maps it at open; later `grow` only retakes a tail previously shrunk. Therefore using newly freed Prefill VRAM for a cache larger than the original `full_slots` requires a larger cache reservation/replacement, unless the original reservation already had the desired full size and had been shrunk. Do not claim `grow()` can exceed the startup reservation.

A replacement transaction must wait/commit decode and refill work; retire every graph and reader that holds old cache addresses; close the old cache; open/fill the larger packed-native cache; rebuild residency mapping and all cache-bound readers; then recapture their graphs before decode resumes. Source owners to audit/rebuild include `Drive`'s cache/base/blob/slot-offset/host-residency bindings, `TokenHits`/`TokenGraph` from `session_capture_token` (captures cache base and `d_res`), `VerifyHits`, each initialized `Verifier` and its copied per-slot offsets/window graphs, and any batch, split/layer, or secondary verifier instances enabled by the chosen route. Main generation has verifier and token-graph setup before Prefill, so those owners currently outlive the prompt boundary. Retire old graph owners before freeing their referenced cache; rebuilding only `ExpertCache` or `Drive` is unsafe. Preserve `SessionState` and its current K/V/GDN/PLE cells, KVG arena, MTP cache/head/state, and 262,144 context; they are not cache backing and should not be reinitialized as part of this transaction. The source audit identifies this as a design seam, not an implemented safe API.

For persistent serving, the existing `VRAM` command already has a narrower in-place cache shrink/grow path within the original segmented reservation. It waits verifier commit, applies pending swaps, device-synchronizes, grows only up to `full_bytes()`, and refills evicted entries that fit. That path preserves slot addresses. It does not establish a way to enlarge the original reservation or bypass graph/owner requirements for cache replacement.

## One-time transfer estimate and token payback

R264's supplied profile arithmetic gives a 128-equivalent cache as 144 slots / 281.03 MiB and a 512-equivalent cache as 624 slots / 1,217.80 MiB. The incremental native payload is 936.77 MiB = 982.28 MB (decimal). At the supplied 6.45 GB/s B570 host-USM H2D rate, payload-only lower bounds are:

| Cache payload | Estimated H2D lower bound |
|---|---:|
| 128-equivalent, 281.03 MiB | 0.046 s |
| 512-equivalent, 1,217.80 MiB | 0.198 s |
| Increment 128→512, 936.77 MiB | 0.152 s |

These estimates assume all listed native payload bytes are copied once at 6.45 GB/s. They exclude source reads, staging, event/dispatch work, allocation, residency-map update, synchronization, and graph teardown/re-capture. They are not observed transition timings; full replacement may incur more than the incremental payload.

For scale only, R264 reports Main-supplied decode rates of 6.29 tok/s (cache128) and 8.48 tok/s (cache512), from different contexts/routes and with output differences, so they do not establish a causal gain. Their per-token wall-time difference is `1/6.29 - 1/8.48 = 0.0411 s/token`; if that difference applied, the incremental-payload lower bound of 0.152 s would be offset after about 4 generated tokens. Gross illustrative saved time is about 0.66 s at 16 tokens, 5.26 s at 128, and 21.0 s at 512, before transaction overhead. Compare measured end-to-end transition cost against paired, same-route decode time before making a cache-growth decision; these arithmetic values are not a performance claim.

## Source and evidence pointers

- `src/program/generate.cpp`: local Prefill and prompt boundary around lines 10,294–10,450 in the reviewed caller; run/refill/map restore/stats precede the decode loop. (The same file also contains server prompt lifecycle and existing `VRAM` command.)
- `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`: public `reset`, no public `release`/`ready`; reset's documented lifecycle.
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:538–560`: queue drains, stager retirement, helper/owned buffer release; `reset` clears implementation and stats.
- `src/core/expert_cache.cpp:~237–310`: `open_sized`, fixed segmented reservation, `close`, bounded `grow`; `include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp` documents fixed `full_slots`/addresses.
- `src/core/session.cpp:1035+`: `session_capture_token`; `src/core/verify.cpp:220+`: `Verifier::init`; `src/program/generate.cpp:4677,4694` and token capture around 4084 show graph/verifier setup that predates the later prompt path.
- Registry v161: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/docs-sycl-storage-retention-20261009/bench/results/2026-10-12-latest-updates-pristine-builds-host-regression/report-registry-v161.json`, 766 entries. Relevant inherited context: R136 cache-expansion ownership, R247 host-USM event/retirement contract, R251, R264 cache-size/rate context, R266 reporting/counter contract.

This is a static source/lifecycle assessment. It does not show that resetting Prefill yields a particular amount of free VRAM, that replacement cache allocation succeeds, or that a larger cache improves decode. Those require a separately authorized, correctly retained measurement with paired correctness and fault evidence.

### Reviewed source hashes

The reviewed HEAD is `0691bcdf5af63a85b3b25650f367d3276db64035`.
